messages:
alex: Hey team — ACME mobile reporting partial chat output over SSE. They get first token/chunk then client shows stream ended. Customer claim: full response exists server-side. Request ID: req_01GZ9XK2HW9T0A1, edge_id: edge_7f3b2c9, region: eu-west-1. App: iOS 17.3 using CF in front. They attached a small log showing final tokens present in our backend but not arriving to client.

sam: Thanks, alex. Can we ask them for a minimal curl repro + tcpdump? Also need the exact HTTP headers they see at their client side. If they can't produce curl, ask for HAR from Safari or a captured nginx access log.

alex: Sent request to customer asking for: 1) curl -N repro (see sample below), 2) client-side headers, 3) any proxy/edge request ids (they already gave edge_7f3b2c9).

sam: Sample curl to suggest to customer: ```curl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream\" -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-small\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hello\"}]}'``` Tell them to replace $TOKEN and include -v so we can see client TLS and tcpsocket behavior.

lina: Also ask them to run this quick node fetch repro if curl is flaky (node 18+): ```
import fetch from 'node-fetch';
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $TOKEN', 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-small', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] }),
});
res.body.on('data', d => console.log('chunk', d.toString()));
``` Helpful to isolate SSE vs client platform buffering.

alex: Customer replied with a short curl - they used `curl --http2` and saw first event then silence, but our backend logs show chunks until EOF. They provided a tcpdump pcap and a few request logs. I uploaded the pcap to the ticket.

sam: Great. From initial look: likely either CF worker or client-side HTTP2 stream windowing. Ask customer to re-run with `--http1.1` to force HTTP/1.1 SSE, and also try `-H \"Connection: keep-alive\" -H \"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\"`. If HTTP/1.1 works then it's HTTP/2 buffering issue.

lina: Another quick check: have them add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and `Cache-Control: no-transform` on any intermediate proxy (if they control it). Some proxies coalesce small chunks. Also ask them to set `Accept: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`.

sre-bot: [auto] Alert: SSE disconnect spikes for customer acme-inc - rate increased 4.6x over baseline in eu-west-1 between 2026-03-15T10:02Z and 2026-03-15T10:12Z. Top edge: edge_7f3b2c9.

sam: Good to have that metric. alex — can you request the following from ACME so we can close loop: 1) curl -N with --http1.1 and --http2 results, 2) HAR or node repro, 3) tcpdump (pcap) with timestamps, 4) client-side headers and UA, 5) any CF worker code if they run one. Also ask them to include our request ID in their fetch to correlate: req_01GZ9XK2HW9T0A1.

alex: Asked for all that — also asked them to try websocket endpoint as a short-term workaround: `wss://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/ws?model=gpt-small`.

lina: If they can reproduce consistently, collect an nginx/edge access log with `request_time`, `upstream_response_time`, `status`, and `body_bytes_sent`. If we see backend sent full body but bytes_sent stops early -> network/proxy. If bytes_sent equals backend total then client likely closed early.

sam: If reproduction shows HTTP/2 only failure, we should escalate to infra team to inspect ALPN/HTTP2 flow control and h2 connection window sizes. Also collect `curl -v` TLS debug lines (`* ALPN, server accepted to use h2`).

alex: Customer just uploaded two pcaps and a HAR. Quick glance: one pcap shows our backend pushing final chunks but no RST from client; there's a pause ~250ms before stream resumes then silence. Might be CF reassembly. Forwarding to CDN contact and flagging for Dedicated customers if needed.

sam: Thanks. Next actions: 1) we ask CDN/edge team to grep edge_7f3b2c9 traces for HTTP/2 frame sizes & WINDOW_UPDATE events, 2) infra to check envoy buffering config between edge and origin, 3) request customer attempt HTTP/1.1 SSE test and websocket fallback.

alex: Noted. I've created debug bundle request in ticket and asked for permissions to download their pcap and HAR. Customer agreed.

lina: One last tip for repro: use `socat` as a raw socket client to see exact byte boundaries. Example: `socat - TCP:api.redwood.example:443,openssl` then paste the raw HTTP payload. Helpful for showing chunk framing.

alex: I'll keep the ticket updated. If we get a clean repro, we'll open a P0 with infra and include collected pcaps, HAR, and request ids. Thanks :thumbsup:

sam: thanks all :rocket:
